# Anshul Dhawan

> Anshul Dhawan is an AI generalist, product leader, and game developer with 12+ years leading growth and monetization for consumer products. He is founder of Social Pixels, an AI-native game studio. He has led product at Supernatural VR (acquired by Meta), VRChat, Glu Mobile / EA, and Zynga.

This is the personal website of Anshul Dhawan, AI generalist, product leader, and game developer. It collects his projects in AI-native games and products, his product leadership background, and his essays on AI, games, and philosophy.

## About

I'm a product leader and the founder of Social Pixels. My career spans software engineering, product leadership, and entrepreneurship, with 12+ years leading growth and monetization for consumer products used by millions. I work across acquisition, engagement, retention, and revenue, partnering with engineering, data, design, and marketing to build products and teams that scale.

At Social Pixels, I launched four social games and built generative AI workflows across the development process, from concept and production to live operations. I also built agentic product analytics workflows that identified bugs, onboarding problems, and frustrating gameplay loops, improving retention by 25% in the first week.

I've led product and growth across VR, subscriptions, and gaming. At VRChat, I owned growth and the expansion to mobile, launching an alpha with creators and players and reducing the app's crash rate by 50%. At Supernatural, acquired by Meta, I led product teams responsible for engagement, subscriber growth, and revenue, and established its analytics and machine learning function.

At VersusGame, I led product, analytics, and design, including an evaluation platform for a fine-tuned LLM product that increased time spent on partner products by 280%. I helped scale the product engineering organization threefold by restructuring it into squads. At Glu Mobile / EA, I led a centralized product group focused on ad optimization and return on ad spend (ROAS), payer conversion, revenue per user, and organic growth, and introduced a career progression framework for product managers.

I started at Zynga as a software engineer building backend systems for Zynga Poker and grew into Head of Product, Growth. I led messaging-platform launches for Words With Friends and the development of Zynga's learning machine, including an experimentation platform that tripled experiment volume and a segmentation tool that increased revenue by 30% for some game studios. For this work, I received Zynga's Spirit Award, which recognizes individuals who go above and beyond their responsibilities to set new standards for the company.

I also founded Equally and raised venture capital to build Da Vinci Club AR, an AI-powered AR learning platform that turned real-world objects into interactive play and reached 100,000 kids. We were semifinalists in the Global Learning XPRIZE. I hold a master's in computer science from USC and have patented work in experimentation and player recommendations.

On nights and weekends, I build projects and hack on new ideas, especially at the intersection of AI and games. I also regularly participate in hackathons.

## Expertise

- AI-native product development
- AI-native game development
- Generative AI and generative games
- Large language model (LLM) evaluation

- Growth and product analytics

## Quick answers

### Who is Anshul Dhawan?

Anshul Dhawan is an AI generalist, product leader, and game developer with 12+ years leading growth and monetization for consumer products. He is founder of Social Pixels, an AI-native game studio. His product leadership roles include VP of Product and Analytics at Supernatural VR, leading product at VRChat, Senior Director of Product and Business Intelligence at Glu Mobile / EA, and Head of Product, Growth at Zynga.

### What makes Anshul Dhawan an AI generalist?

He works across engineering, product, growth, analytics, and game design, and applies AI across that whole stack instead of in a single discipline. At Social Pixels, AI produced the concept art, 3D assets, characters, game code, and server code for Network Cities, and the studio achieved 20x improvements in production cost and time-to-market. He also builds LLM evaluation tools, such as a poker tournament that pits Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok against each other, and writes about how companies become AI-native organizations.

### What product leadership experience does Anshul Dhawan have?

He was VP of Product and Analytics at Supernatural VR, which Meta acquired in a deal reported at about $400M. He led product at VRChat, one of the defining social VR platforms, and was Senior Director of Product and Business Intelligence at Glu Mobile / EA. He spent more than seven years at Zynga, rising from software engineer to Head of Product, Growth, where he led the development of Zynga's experimentation and optimization service.

### What games has Anshul Dhawan built?

He built Network Cities, an AI-native city builder that reached 200,000 players and $20,000 in revenue; an open-world adventure experiment that combines a deterministic simulation with real-time generative video instead of a game engine; and Words with Degens, a word-scramble game played with friends and launched on play.fun. At Zynga he built live-game infrastructure, including a server-side experimentation service and a skill-based player matchmaking system, both covered by U.S. patent filings.

### What is Anshul Dhawan working on now?

He is founder of Social Pixels, where he builds AI-powered games and product analytics workflows. On nights and weekends, he builds projects, experiments with new ideas, and regularly participates in hackathons.

### Has Anshul Dhawan spoken at industry conferences?

Yes. At GDC 2016 he presented "Evaluating Game Experiments: A More Robust Approach for Freemium Games," a more reliable method for evaluating free-to-play game experiments that accounts for the behavior of the most engaged players.

### What does Anshul Dhawan write about?

He writes about AI-native organizations, generative games, the case for being a generalist, decision-making, and philosophy.

## Projects

- [Can You Make an Open World Adventure Game Like GTA Without a Game Engine?](https://anshuldhawan.com/projects/open-world-adventure-without-a-game-engine/): A playable experiment combining a deterministic simulation with real-time generative video. (Builder · AI-native game · Generative video · 2026)
- [Can You Build a Time Machine with AI?](https://anshuldhawan.com/projects/can-you-build-a-time-machine-with-ai/): On turning a city and a year into a world you can explore, and what happens when you look around the corner. (Builder · AI-native experiment · Generative worlds · 2026)
- [Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini vs Grok — Poker Tournament](https://anshuldhawan.com/projects/poker-tournament/): A Texas Hold'em evaluation harness that pits frontier LLMs against each other across hands and tournaments. (Builder · LLM evaluation · 2026)
- [Network Cities](https://anshuldhawan.com/projects/network-cities/): An AI-native city builder that went from a rough Three.js prototype to 200,000 players and $20,000 in revenue. (Founder · Social Pixels · AI-native game · 2025)
- [Da Vinci Club AR](https://anshuldhawan.com/projects/da-vinci-club-ar/): A computer-vision-based AR app for kids that turned the world around them into a learning surface. (Builder · AR · EdTech)
- [Experimentation & Optimization Service](https://anshuldhawan.com/projects/experimentation-service/): Server-side experimentation and optimization service for Zynga that let PMs and analysts ship experiments without engineering bottlenecks. (Product · Zynga · Platform · 2014 — 2017)
- [Words with Degens](https://anshuldhawan.com/projects/words-with-degens/): A scramble game you play with friends, built around crypto lingo. Launched on play.fun with on-chain rewards for winners. (Builder · Game · crypto · 2025)
- [Global Learning XPrize](https://anshuldhawan.com/projects/global-learning-xprize/): Semi-finalist in the $15M Global Learning XPrize, a competition for teams building software to teach literacy and numeracy to kids without access to schools or teachers. (Builder · EdTech · Semi-finalist · 2017)
- [Player Recommendation System](https://anshuldhawan.com/projects/player-recommendation/): A skill-based matchmaking system that pairs players for more balanced and engaging sessions. (Product · Zynga · Matchmaking · 2013)

## Writings

- [The Age of the Artist-Entrepreneur](https://anshuldhawan.com/writings/the-age-of-the-artist-entrepreneur/): On AI, the rise of micro businesses, and a world where everyone can turn an idea into something real. (Technology, 2026-09)
- [The Tussle Between the Brain and the Soul](https://anshuldhawan.com/writings/the-tussle-between-the-brain-and-the-soul/): Let the soul lead the creation. Let the brain lead the distribution. (Philosophy, 2026-09)
- [AI Native Organization](https://anshuldhawan.com/writings/ai-native-organization/): On the stack, org design, and operating habits required to become AI Native. (Technology, 2026-05)
- [What is Spirituality?](https://anshuldhawan.com/writings/what-is-spirituality/): On spirit, identity, meditation, gratitude, affirmations, and living consciously. (Philosophy, 2025-11)
- [Emotion and Rationality in Decision-Making](https://anshuldhawan.com/writings/emotion-and-rationality-of-decision-making/): On using emotion as signal and rationality as refinement. (Philosophy, 2025-09)
- [The issue of neat categorization](https://anshuldhawan.com/writings/the-issue-of-neat-categorization/): On why categories help us think, and what they quietly leave out. (Philosophy, 2025-07)
- [Three Perspectives on Reality](https://anshuldhawan.com/writings/three-perspectives-on-reality/): On moving between broad, close, and metaphysical views of reality. (Philosophy, 2025-04)
- [Generative Games on building systems that generate games](https://anshuldhawan.com/writings/generative-games/): On building systems that generate games, and what that changes about the medium. (Technology, 2025-01)
- [A generalist's case for staying a generalist](https://anshuldhawan.com/writings/generalist-case/): Notes on optimizing for breadth in a world that keeps asking you to specialize. (Philosophy, 2024-09)

## Talks
